verdict.rationale: Keycloak is a self-managed server. First-party docs cover running it from a container image, installing it on Kubernetes or OpenShift with the Operator, clustering instances, putting it behind your own reverse proxy, and switching to a production database such as PostgreSQL. User data can also stay in your own LDAP or Active Directory, or in a custom relational store via a provider, and community users confirm long-running self-hosted, clustered and on-prem deployments. Missing for 10: detailed first-party database configuration and supported-database documentation in the evidence (only a one-line PostgreSQL mention); hands-on reports (e.g. OpenShift difficulties) show self-hosting can be operationally demanding.
